chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, he said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he heard him saying:

You will continue to wait until you become like the frightened goat, upon which the butcher does not care where he places his hand. You will have no honor by which you are honored, nor a support to which you refer your affairs.

key_terms.الْجَازِرُ: The butcher, representing those who may test or determine the fate of the community
key_terms.الْمَعْزِ الْمَهُولَةِ: The frightened goat, a metaphor for the vulnerable and uncertain state of the Shia
key_terms.سَنَدٌ: Support or backbone, referring to the deputies or the Imam himself as a reference for affairs
key_terms.شَرَفٌ: Honor or prestige, referring to the status provided by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'frightened goat' metaphor in Shia eschatology regarding the Great Occultation?
ai.summary: Al-Nu'mani records this narration from Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) to illustrate the state of *al-intizar* (waiting) during the Minor and Major Gheibah, where the community lacks a definitive political and spiritual anchor. The metaphor of the 'frightened goat' (*al-ma'z al-mahulah*) signifies a loss of dignity and agency, as the Imam's absence leaves the Shia vulnerable to external pressures and internal disarray without a central authority to guide their affairs.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (5) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abul Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan that Abul Jarood had heard Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) saying: “You still wait until you become like frightened goats that the butcher does not care on which of he puts his hand.

You will be of no honor and no supporter, to whom you refer your affairs.” Have these traditions referred save to the disappearance of the imam of deliverance, who is the honor, with which the Shia are honored, and to the disappearance of the means (the deputies) between him and his Shia? Are the deputies not the supporters, whom the Shia refer their affairs to during the disappearance of their imam (as) to be delivered to the imam? By losing the imam and the means between them and their imam, the Shia become like the goats subjected to the test to be tried that which of them is to perish and which of them is to be saved. These are what I have in my mind of traditions concerning the disappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (aj), whereas there are so much many other traditions talking about the subject.
